wins.text: Net income of $4 billion, EPS of $1.96, ROTCE of 8.7% on $21.7B revenue; total revenues up 8% YoY with positive operating leverage at each of the 5 businesses
Markets revenues up 16% — best Q2 since 2020; Equities had best Q2 ever with prime balances hitting a record, up ~27% YoY
Banking revenues up 18%; Investment banking fees up 13% with M&A up 52%; involved in 7 of top 10 IB fee events YTD
Wealth revenues up 20% with pretax margin of 29%; client investment assets grew 17% YoY; generated positive operating leverage for 5th consecutive quarter
Returned over $3B in capital to common shareholders in Q2 including $2B in buybacks; increased quarterly dividend to $0.60/share; announced at least $4B in Q3 buybacks under $20B repurchase program

risks.text: ACL build of ~$600M in the quarter driven by transfer risk in Russia (unremittable client dividends) and corporate portfolio growth in Markets and Banking; corporate nonaccrual loans increased due to idiosyncratic downgrades
Wealth net new investment asset inflows slowed in Q2 as clients were cautious amid macro uncertainty; management acknowledged clients remain in 'wait and see' mode
Retail Services revenues declined 5% due to lower partner sales activity and higher partner payments from lower net credit losses; macro uncertainty weighing on commercial card spend (flat YoY)
Goods prices expected to start rising over summer as tariffs take effect; management noted pauses in CapEx and hiring among client base; tariff and trade policy uncertainty remains a key macro risk

Transformation expenses increasing meaningfully in 2025 vs. $3B in 2024; OCC consent order remediation ongoing with data plan still in early remediation phase; elevated severance (~$600M forecast for full year 2025)

guidance_items.detail: Now expect to be at the higher end of full-year revenue range, around $84B, up from prior midpoint guidance
NII ex-Markets expected up closer to 4% for full year 2025
Full-year expenses expected around $53.4B; higher if revenues exceed $84B
Branded Cards NCL rate guided to 3.5%-4%; Retail Services NCL rate guided to 5.75%-6.25%
At least $4B in share buybacks in Q3 2025 under $20B repurchase program; dividend increased to $0.60/share beginning Q3

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Stablecoin disruption risk to Services/cross-border revenues and competitive dynamics with non-bank entrants like Circle
Specific dollar quantum of transformation expenses in Q2 and run-rate going forward
Whether 13.1% year-end CET1 target remains appropriate given SCB relief and regulatory reform trajectory
